w7-q7: Incorrect — In a traditional network control is distributed, not held by a centralized controller; that is the SDN approach.
Correct — Protocols like OSPF execute at the individual switches, which forward traffic in a distributed manner without central control.
Incorrect — End-user devices do not run the network's routing protocol logic.
Incorrect — Routing protocols run on network devices, not in the cloud.
w7-q8: Incorrect — 2006 is not the year OpenFlow was presented at ACM SIGCOMM.
Correct — OpenFlow, the origin of the SDN idea, was presented at ACM SIGCOMM in 2008.
Incorrect — 2009 is when the OpenFlow V1.0.0 specification was published, a year after the SIGCOMM presentation.
Incorrect — 2011 is not the year OpenFlow was presented at ACM SIGCOMM.
w7-q9: Correct — With no matching flow-rule, the switch sends a PACKET-IN message to the controller, which then installs a suitable rule.
Incorrect — FLOW-REQUEST is not the OpenFlow message a switch sends on a table miss.

Incorrect — CONTROL-SYNC is not the message a switch sends for an unmatched packet.
w7-q10: Incorrect — The Northbound API connects the control layer to the application layer, not to the infrastructure layer.
Correct — The Southbound API links the control layer and the infrastructure layer, using the OpenFlow protocol.
Incorrect — East-Westbound APIs relate to communication between controllers, not control-to-infrastructure communication.
Incorrect — North-Southbound API is not the standard name for the control-to-infrastructure interface.
